:::{#sol-min-and-argmin}

1. The square of a real number is never negative,
   so $(x - 2)^2 \ge 0$ for every $x$,
   and therefore $f(x) \ge 0 + 1 = 1$.
   The square is $0$ only when $x - 2 = 0$,
   that is, when $x = 2$,
   and there $f(2) = 1$.
   So the smallest value of $f$ is $1$,
   and $x = 2$ is the only input where $f$ takes it.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{.solution}

2. Evaluate $g$ at each of its four inputs:

   | $x$    | $0$ | $1$ | $3$ | $4$ |
   |--------|-----|-----|-----|-----|
   | $g(x)$ | $5$ | $2$ | $2$ | $5$ |

   The smallest value of $g$ is $2$,
   and $g$ takes it at two inputs, $x = 1$ and $x = 3$.
   The answer to "where?" is the set $\cb{1, 3}$,
   not a single number.

:::
